evidence_summary: IFRA defines Woody by explicitly describing woody notes as a large odor family that includes sandalwood and cedarwood facets.
IFF labels ingredient entries with Woody under its Olfactive Family field, confirming category-level use rather than one ingredient identity.
IFRA calls Green a broad descriptor and uses the expression green notes within the definition.
IFF uses Green as an Olfactive Family label for fragrance ingredients.
IFRA states that floral notes belong to the large floral family and can represent single or multi-faceted flower character.
IFF uses Floral as an Olfactive Family label for fragrance ingredients.
IFRA defines Citrus notes through the smell of fruit from the citrus family, including orange, lemon and grapefruit.
IFF uses Citrus as an Olfactive Family label; the P0 form differs only by plural labeling at the scent-category level.
IFRA contains 20 Blackcurrant descriptor rows and 6 Cassis principal-name variants whose descriptors include Blackcurrant.
IFF explicitly pairs Blackcurrant with cassis in the olfactive description of Damascone Delta.
IFF lists multiple Blackcurrant Bud natural materials from Ribes nigrum, supporting a concept-to-material-family distinction.
IFRA defines Musk-Like broadly and applies it as the primary descriptor to 62 diverse ingredient rows with varied secondary facets.
IFF describes Edenolide as a powdery, creamy, warm white musk and says it contributes soft musk qualities, supporting White Musk as a specific musk profile rather than the whole class.
IFRA lists 5 Agarwood oil/extract variants across 3 CAS values, all with Woody, Animal Like and Smoky descriptors.

Givaudan's Agarwood Oil page explains Aquilaria resin as agarwood and uses oud for the prized perfumery concept on that same material page; this supports term-level equivalence, not identity with one oil.
IFRA contains 19 Cedarwood principal-name variants across 10 CAS values and 48 Cedarwood descriptor rows.
Givaudan identifies Virginia cedarwood oil as Juniperus virginiana, CAS 8000-27-9, with a woody, spicy and dry profile.
IFF identifies Cedarwood Oil Extra as Cupressus funebris wood oil with distinct CAS values and a cedarwood, balsamic-sweet description.
IFF separately lists Cedarwood Oil Atlas from Cedrus atlantica, demonstrating another botanical cedarwood material under the woody family.
